scope: Semantic normalization review of the currently present vendor bundles in vendors/*.json, focused on catalog, inventory, customers/loyalty, staff permissions, cash closeout, reporting and multilocation. Alias groups identify comparable merchant-observable jobs while retaining the original claims; collisions record superficially similar claims that must not be unified. No vendor behavior was tested.

alias_groups.rationale: Each documents merchant configuration of a sellable catalog entry or its selectable form: product/variant, item variation, menu item, or POS item.
alias_groups.variant_cautions: Shopify and Square model variants with option values and per-variant details; Toast describes a hierarchical restaurant menu; BTCPay POS item documentation gives title/price/description/image but not variants. Do not infer common SKU, modifier, price, or inventory semantics.

alias_groups.rationale: Both let a merchant represent selectable product variants/options and retain values on the resulting variant records.
alias_groups.variant_cautions: Shopify supports named options and variant-level values, bulk combinations and category metafield links; Square applies reusable option sets to generate fixed variations. Their limits and import/price workflows differ. Toast modifiers are add-ons/choices, not equivalent stock-bearing variants.

alias_groups.rationale: Both document bulk ingestion/update of catalog records from structured files rather than editing each item individually.
alias_groups.variant_cautions: Shopify uses product CSV with variants and separate multi-location inventory CSV; Square uses a mapped item-library import with row errors. Cancellation, rollback and supported columns differ.

alias_groups.rationale: Both allow export of product/catalog data to a structured file for offline review or migration.
alias_groups.variant_cautions: Shopify export covers products/variants and has distinct inventory exports; Square can export a filtered item library. Do not assume equivalent columns or round-trip fidelity.

alias_groups.rationale: Each documents an operator changing recorded item stock quantity or availability through an adjustment/quick-edit surface.
alias_groups.variant_cautions: Shopify Quick counts has POS and admin paths; Square requires tracked stock and a reason; Toast distinguishes In Stock, Out of Stock and remaining Quantity and has Web/POS manager surfaces. Approval, audit history, location scope and decrement behavior differ.

alias_groups.rationale: Each documents counting physical on-hand inventory and using the count to reconcile recorded stock.
alias_groups.variant_cautions: Shopify documents scheduled, staff-attributed counts with manager review; Square separates cycle counts (uncounted items unchanged) from full counts. Square submission/approval and Shopify update timing differ.

alias_groups.rationale: Both document creation of a stock transfer between locations with products/quantities and a transfer record.
alias_groups.variant_cautions: Shopify supports draft and shipment lifecycle details; Square documents source/destination, tracking and draft/create/export. Do not infer identical reservation or stock-decrement timing.

alias_groups.rationale: The claim documents the origin location preparing/scanning quantities and sending an admin-created transfer shipment.
alias_groups.variant_cautions: No Square claim in the reviewed bundle documents the same send/fulfill step at this granularity; keep this as a one-vendor normalized behavior until evidence supports an alias.

alias_groups.rationale: Both let destination staff record receipt of transferred goods, including quantity reconciliation and full or partial acceptance.
alias_groups.variant_cautions: Shopify supports accepting all or reviewing/counting line items and accept/reject behavior; Square documents full/partial receipt and may permit instant transfer. Exception handling and inventory posting timing differ.

alias_groups.rationale: Both document creating a customer profile in connection with merchant activity or through a customer-management workflow.
alias_groups.variant_cautions: Shopify POS creation collects at least one identity field and separately records marketing consent; Square also supports import, matching and failed-row recovery. Creation does not imply cart attachment, consent, loyalty enrollment or the same required fields.

alias_groups.rationale: Each documents configuring or assigning a staff/user access profile that governs some merchant or POS actions.
alias_groups.variant_cautions: Shopify POS Pro roles gate actions and can require manager approval; Square uses configurable permission sets; Toast groups permissions into jobs; BTCPay documents role names/invitation or API assignment but not a full action matrix. Treat BTCPay role names as labels, not equivalent permissions.

alias_groups.rationale: Both document creating a retail location record in the merchant account.
alias_groups.variant_cautions: Shopify describes default fulfillment availability and zero stock for new products at the location; Square claim describes entering profile/contact details. Neither should be conflated with BTCPay's additional payment stores or Toast hierarchy entities.

alias_groups.rationale: Both describe choosing/switching the location context used by a POS device and its scoped activity.
alias_groups.variant_cautions: Shopify associates POS device location with tax context and Pro subscription; Square switches location-specific catalog/report/device context. Access and subscription rules are product-specific.

alias_groups.rationale: Each documents ending/closing a cash handling interval and comparing or recording actual cash against expected activity.
alias_groups.variant_cautions: Shopify sessions hold opening float, cash movement and final count; Square can end a drawer with an actual count; Toast has explicit open/paused/closed states and blind/full expected-balance permissions. Session boundaries and variance calculations differ.

alias_groups.rationale: Each documents establishing or configuring a cash drawer/register with a starting cash float for later reconciliation.
alias_groups.variant_cautions: Shopify sets starting float at register session; Square starts a session from POS and requires the Cash Management add-on; Toast configures default starting balance and physical drawer/device cash mode. Toast's cited claim is configuration, not proof of the same session-start UI.

alias_groups.rationale: Each provides auditable entry of cash moving into or out of an active drawer outside an ordinary sale payment.
alias_groups.variant_cautions: Square exposes generic Pay In/Pay Out with description; Toast separates Cash In, Cash Collected, payout, tip out and cash drop, with different limits/reasons and audit records.

alias_groups.rationale: Each exposes cash activity or discrepancy information to support drawer/deposit reconciliation.
alias_groups.variant_cautions: Shopify reports register-session discrepancies and cash payments; Toast drawer screens expose balances/activity while deposit reports diagnose expected versus actual deposits. These are related reports, not the same metric or closeout workflow.

alias_groups.rationale: Each provides an export/print/email path for operational report data or configurable export fields.
alias_groups.variant_cautions: Shopify exports/remote-closes register sessions; Toast configures export datasets and columns; Square exports or emails eligible reports with report-specific restrictions. This is an interaction-level alias only; data coverage and file schemas are not equivalent.

collisions.reason: Do not collapse these into one stock-tracking guarantee. BTCPay-C024 documents only an optional quantity field in POS configuration; it does not establish decrement, reservation, restock or oversell prevention. SQO-C035 documents decrement after supported sales. SHO-C001 describes channel synchronization, not precise decrement rules. Toast claims document stock status/count controls, not necessarily automatic decrement.

A BTCPay store is a payment/configuration boundary and can be created more than once; it is not documented as a physical location with shared inventory. Shopify/Square location records and Toast enterprise hierarchy ownership have different inventory, tax and access semantics.

Role assignment governs account/store access; BTCPay multisig Owner requirement is a signer-participant setup constraint with key-spend implications. Do not normalize multisig ownership to an employee permission profile.

Employee roles and permission sets constrain staff actions in a merchant POS. Square SDK OAuth scopes authorize an integration to call seller/account APIs; they do not assign cashier or manager permissions.

Shopify's claim displays a third-party loyalty status field; Square claims configure/operate points and rewards; BTCPay claims manage subscription plans and prepaid credits. These do not represent equivalent loyalty earning, redemption or customer-account behavior.

Explicit staff-entered profile creation, name-only chip-card recognition, automatic guest/contact/order-history capture and customer import are distinct triggers, data sets and consent/privacy surfaces. Do not merge as generic customer creation.

These Square claims use distinct IDs but describe the same cash drawer history/session detail view with substantially overlapping fields and filters. Treat as a likely duplicate claim pair for integration cleanup, not two independent vendor capabilities.

BTCPay-C033 is an on-chain Bitcoin payout signed/broadcast from a wallet; Toast-C018 and Square-C038 are physical cash drawer removals or register adjustments. BTCPay-C033 is also categorized cash_closeout, which is semantically misleading; normalize it under payout/wallet transaction operations, not cash drawer closeout.

The claims cover different report units and scopes: Bitcoin wallet transactions/product quantities/payments; Shopify POS daily/staff sales; Square restaurant close-of-day; Toast product-mix and location-scoped reports. A shared reporting label does not establish equivalent metrics, timing or reconciliation. BTCPay-C018 itself bundles multiple distinct report types and should be split before strict one-report-per-claim normalization.

Shopify/Square variants generally carry distinct product option/variation records; Toast modifier groups model choices or add-ons with selection constraints/inheritance; Square modifier behavior controls prompt/receipt presentation. Do not merge modifiers with stock-bearing product variants.

Creation, origin shipment and destination receipt are separate merchant-observable steps. Shopify documents a shipment lifecycle and destination verification; Square documents transfer creation and receiving with possible instant transfer. Do not reduce all steps to a single transfer capability or assume identical stock posting time.

Square's documented POS option is Lightning acceptance with custodial Square wallet/balance settlement and gift-card-only refund behavior; BTCPay claims describe merchant-configured Bitcoin wallet receipt and on-chain PSBT payout. Do not imply these are the same Bitcoin rail, custody model, refund method or reporting record, or that Square provides on-chain self-custody acceptance.

Products-sold quantities, inventory-count variance exports, sales ranking and multi-location product-mix comparisons are different measures and event bases. Do not infer that a sales report equals a stock ledger or an inventory count.

notes: Aliases are candidate semantic keys for later integration; preserve vendor claim IDs, qualifiers, plan/version gates, payment rail, device conditions, permissions and failure behavior in the normalized record.
No alias was created for BTCPay POS quantity field and tracked inventory decrement, BTCPay prepaid subscriptions and loyalty, or BTCPay additional stores and retail locations.

BTCPay's public user guide documents Bitcoin wallet choice and invoice status; Square's Bitcoin claims use a Lightning rail and Square custody/settlement options. Never import the custodial Square mechanism or gift-card refund rule into an OpenBMT Bitcoin capability claim.

Cash drawer session tracking, cash drawer movement entry, deposits, shift review, close-of-day reporting and Bitcoin wallet payouts are separate merchant jobs. A generic cash-closeout or payout key would erase material workflow differences.

Reporting claims are especially broad in some bundles. BTCPay-C018, Shopify-SHO-C014, Square-SQO-C011/SQO-C012 and Toast-TOO-C027/TOO-C028/TOO-C036 bundle multiple metrics, delivery modes or scope rules; preserve those distinctions or split claims before claiming report parity.

Customer profiles, consent, card-name recognition, automatic guest data capture, loyalty status, loyalty rewards and subscription access must remain separate concepts because their triggers, data, consent, custody and customer outcomes differ.

The current scan included every vendor JSON present during this review, including Shopify and Toast operation bundles. If a vendor bundle changes after this review, rerun normalization for that bundle before final integration.
